sections.content: The futuro simple is formed by adding the same endings to the infinitive. The endings are -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis and -án. For example: *viajaré*, *viajarás*, *viajará*, *viajaremos*, *viajarán*. Unlike the pretérito indefinido, the infinitive stays complete before the ending. Use this form to talk about future actions.

items.english: They will live in another city.

sections.content: These endings aren't arbitrary — they grew out of the present tense of *haber* (*he, has, ha...*) fused onto the infinitive, which is also why they're identical across *-ar*, *-er* and *-ir* verbs instead of three separate sets.
